biography: Cleveland Soares Jr., a name synonymous with unpredictable brilliance in the vibrant world of Brazilian motorsports, hails from the bustling streets of São Paulo. His journey began not in a kart, but behind the wheel of his father's beat-up Puma GTB, delivering produce across the city's chaotic marketplaces. It was during these high-speed runs, dodging potholes and weaving through traffic, that Cleveland honed his raw talent, a talent that caught the eye of a local Copa Fusca team owner after witnessing him drift a corner on two wheels while avoiding a stray dog. While his early years showed promise, inconsistency plagued his career. One moment he's a podium contender, the next he's spinning out in the first lap. Now a veteran, Cleveland remains a beloved figure, a reminder that passion and audacity can sometimes triumph over meticulous planning, even if it's just for a fleeting, glorious moment.
drivingStyle: Cleveland's driving style is a chaotic symphony of aggression and finesse. He attacks corners with a ferocity that often borders on reckless, relying on instinct and raw car control to wrestle the machine into submission. Tire management is an afterthought, a casualty of his 'pedal to the metal' philosophy. Under pressure, Cleveland either cracks spectacularly or pulls off a miraculous overtake, a testament to his inconsistent nature.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles - Albuquerque's calculated precision versus Soares' impulsive aggression.
A fierce on-track battle for position during the 2018 Copa Fusca championship led to accusations of blocking and unsportsmanlike conduct.
Souza publicly criticized Soares' driving style, calling it 'dangerous and irresponsible,' sparking a war of words that continues to this day.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific samba song before every race, claiming it 'unleashes his inner beast'.
Refuses to look at the starting grid before the race, believing it 'jinxes' his chances.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being perfect, it's about being brave enough to make mistakes and still floor it."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Copa Fusca race at Interlagos, after starting last due to a qualifying mishap, a true testament to his raw skill.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2019 Puma GTB championship decider, handing the title to his arch-rival, Ricardo Albuquerque.
